newsitem.title: USA: Former pitching ace Denny McLain sentenced to 8 years.
newsitem.headline: Former pitching ace Denny McLain sentenced to 8 years.

text.p: Denny McLain, the former Detroit Tiger pitching star and two-time Cy Young Award winner, was sentenced to eight years and one month in jail Wednesday for stealing $3 million in pension money from a now defunct meat-packing company.
McLain, the last 30 game winner in the major leagues, and a business partner were convicted of theft, consipiracy money-laundering and mail-fraud by a federal jury in December.

On Wednesday, U.S. Distict Court Judge Patrick Duggan ordered McLain to serve 57 months for three of the counts and 97 months for two of the counts, said a spokeswoman for the judge. All of the jail time will be served concurrently.
McLain and his former partner Roger Smigiel were also ordered to repay restitution of $2.5 million, plus interest dating back to Feb. 18, 1994. Smigiel received a seven-year jail sentence.
McLain is expected to report for prison in about six weeks, his lawyer said.

McLain won 31 games in 1968 as he led the Tigers to a World Series championship. After retiring from baseball, McLain was convicted of racketeering, extortion and cocaine possession in 1985. He served 2 1/2 years of his 23-year sentence after an appeals court ruled he had not received a fair trial.

In the current case, prosecutors said McLain and his partners raided the $12.5 million pension fund of Peet Packing Co. of Chesaning, Mich., after buying the company in 1994. They used the money to repay loans used to buy the business, a country club membership and a condominium in Puerto Rico, according to prosecutors.
Peat Packing closed in June 1995, putting about 200 people out of work.
